scope: Review of all 19 supplied PDFs, focused on methods, objectives, empirical evidence and relevant appendices. This is not a line-by-line verification of every appendix proof. Original PDFs remain unchanged. Proposed transfers and algebraic audits below are our analysis, not reported speech results.

papers.title: Variational generalized nonlinear mode decomposition: Algorithm and applications
papers.method: Generalizes modes to time-domain chirps and frequency-domain dispersive components with explicit support intervals. Fuses time-frequency maps, clusters ridges, identifies coordinate direction, and initializes variational demodulation or dispersion compensation.
papers.evidence: Synthetic mixtures and noise tests; bat echolocation and railway vibration applications. The paper explicitly assumes separated time-frequency ridges and says its method fails when crossing/close ridges violate that condition.
papers.limit: No compact parameter transmission or speech coding experiment. Demodulated amplitude/phase trajectories remain functions, not automatically short vectors. The ridge classification and thresholds are algorithmic choices.
papers.proposal: Generate programs for demodulated quadrature envelopes or phase innovations; test a frequency-domain representation for transient modes. Count carrier, support boundaries, coordinate choice, and envelope coefficients. Select by achieved description/error, not ridge-type rules alone.

papers.title: TFD-Net: Towards Intelligent Time-Frequency Mode Decomposition with Practical Applications
papers.method: Complex multi-resolution convolutional transforms and residual U-Net features feed a query-based segmentation model. Hungarian matching supervises individual instantaneous-frequency tracks. Extracted tracks initialize a separate iterative demodulation reconstruction procedure.
papers.evidence: 30,000 training, 1,000 validation and 200 test synthetic modulated signals, length 256, one to six modes. BCE/Dice losses supervise maps and masks. Real examples are power-system oscillations and bat echolocation.
papers.limit: The existing training does not optimize the size of a transmitted expression. Its conclusion identifies unfolded reconstruction as future work; it should not be described as already a fully neural end-to-end waveform decomposition.
papers.proposal: Borrow permutation-invariant query slots and frequency-track proposals to initialize VMD-like optimization. Add actual program reconstruction and complexity objectives; validate on speech and variable mode counts.

papers.title: FINER: Flexible spectral-bias tuning in Implicit NEural Representation by Variable-periodic Activation Functions
papers.venue: Local arXiv v1 manuscript; FINER conference line
papers.method: Uses sin((abs(x)+1)*x) and wider bias initialization to expose different oscillation scales while retaining the base weight initialization. Studies spectral bias through geometry and empirical neural tangent kernels.
papers.evidence: Image fitting, signed-distance fields and radiance fields. Image comparison uses three hidden layers with 256 neurons each; varying bias initialization changes recoverable detail.
papers.limit: This PDF is the original FINER preprint, not FINER++. Its reported improvements do not establish few-constant IMF coding, nor a generally optimal functional family. Initialization still affects convergence.
papers.proposal: Use variable-periodic composition as an optional expression primitive and fit small explicit programs, with initialization as a separate factor. Compare after expanding the primitive into elementary operations so it does not receive an artificially cheap code.

papers.title: Recent Advances in Symbolic Regression
papers.method: Surveys deterministic enumeration/programming, genetic programming, semantic search, neural generators, equation learners and hybrids. Distinguishes trees, graphs, grammar and reusable subexpressions; discusses accuracy, interpretability and computation separately.
papers.evidence: A methodological survey, not a new speech experiment. Describes variable projection, semantic replacement, graph reuse, neural guidance and sparsity-based equation learning across the literature.
papers.limit: A survey description is not independent experimental validation of each cited method. General benchmark success cannot establish compact speech representations or global optimality of numerical fits.
papers.proposal: Replace isolated complete-tree proposals with neural-guided local edits and a reusable program graph. Benchmark generator, fitter and grammar independently, with both proposal and wall-time budgets.

papers.title: Density-Based Adaptive Mode Decomposition
papers.method: Uses weighted spectral meanshift with bandwidth selection to determine frequency partitions and mode counts. Direct extraction uses disjoint masks; optional hybrid refinement initializes VMD from clustering results.
papers.evidence: Synthetic signals and real examples including TIMIT speech. Reported timing: direct extraction 2.4 s, hybrid refinement 20.7 s, VMD 14.0 s for the stated comparison. Discussion calls the method a frequency-domain partitioning framework rather than a generative intrinsic time-domain mode model.
papers.limit: Perfect reconstruction of uncompressed transform partitions is not parameter compression. The unrestricted VMD/clustering equivalence is not established by constructing hard partitions; see our algebraic counterexample below. Number of clusters remains sensitive to representation and bandwidth.
papers.proposal: Use density clustering as an initializer and candidate split/merge proposal, then accept mode counts based on actual compact-program reconstruction. Keep hard masks and soft VMD updates as distinct ablation arms.

papers.title: FINER++: Building a Family of Variable-periodic Functions for Activating Implicit Neural Representation
papers.method: Extends variable-periodic construction to sine, Gaussian and complex wavelet activations. Bias range controls the used portion of the activation; discusses overlap/degeneration and progressive streamable representations.
papers.evidence: Visual signal fitting and rendering, including a progressively widened network with earlier parameters frozen. A representative network has three layers and 256 neurons per layer. The author-version header says final edited content may change.
papers.limit: The local PDF is FINER++, separate from P03. Extra initialization and scale parameters remain. Visual accuracy and a streamable neural network do not establish a compact symbolic IMF representation.
papers.proposal: Learn or search compact compositions with chirped/localized primitives, and progressively refine only unresolved structure. Preserve a fully explicit evaluable program; charge every per-IMF weight if an INR is used directly.

papers.title: KAN: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
papers.method: Learns spline functions on graph edges with summation nodes; supports grid refinement, sparsification, pruning and subsequent symbolic substitution.
papers.evidence: Mathematical/physical regression and PDE examples. The approximation theorem assumes sufficiently smooth compositional edge functions. Appendix M fits affine transforms around user-specified symbolic functions via grid search and regression.
papers.limit: KAN does not automatically output an arbitrary shortest symbolic function. Its symbolification uses a user-defined candidate library. Splines, grids and weights have storage cost; for one input variable, the multivariate representation theorem is not the core advantage.
papers.proposal: Use a small adaptive spline/compositional network as a teacher to expose useful structure, then distill into explicit programs and re-evaluate. Also keep sparse splines as a direct, fully costed representation.

papers.title: RAG-SR: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Neural Symbolic Regression
papers.method: Semantic descent removes a feature's contribution and generates/retrieves a replacement from the residual. A dynamic library stores evaluated subtrees and their outputs; a neural generator conditions on residual and a retrieved expression.
papers.evidence: Synthetic tree generation and 120 black-box regression datasets; separate Feynman/Strogatz results in appendix. Default evolutionary model has ten trees, population 200 and 100 generations. Retrieval restricts replacement size; full RAG-SR is slower than TPSR in their implementation.
papers.limit: The model is multi-feature symbolic regression, not short speech IMF coding. Edit distance to a generating tree is not our primary objective. Residual addition without replacement can bloat descriptions.
papers.proposal: Condition expression edits on the current curve and its residual, not only raw IMF samples. Reuse good subexpressions, replace rather than blindly append, and retrain on actual successful speech-derived fits. Keep test speakers out of the training library.

papers.title: Symbolic Regression via MDLformer-Guided Search: From Minimizing Prediction Error to Minimizing Description Length
papers.method: Learns a predictor of simplified formula token length from numeric observations, with numeric/symbolic alignment pretraining, then uses it to guide search for useful subformulas.
papers.evidence: 133 known-formula and 122 black-box problems. Appendix: about 131 million generated data/formula pairs, 31.9M numeric-model parameters, 41 hours on eight A100 GPUs.
papers.limit: Its MDL target is simplified symbolic length, not a measured audio payload including numerical precision. SymPy-based simplification is not proof of the globally shortest representation. Estimated complexity may fail out of distribution; it is a guide, not an optimality certificate.
papers.proposal: Train a smaller speech-specific predictor of remaining error-versus-description cost from actual search archives. Periodically verify rankings using the real fitter, retain uncertainty/exploration, and never accept a claimed compression result solely from the surrogate.

papers.title: MAPSS: Manifold-based Assessment of Perceptual Source Separation
papers.method: Embeds references, distorted references and separated outputs with pretrained audio representations and diffusion maps. Defines distinct perceptual match and separation scores with uncertainty/truncation analyses.
papers.evidence: SEBASS: over 900 separated signals, about 11,000 ratings, 10-second outputs judged by 15 raters. No new listening study; fine-frame outputs are aggregated to compare with utterance-level human scores.
papers.limit: Not validated as an isolated-IMF or isolated-40-ms speech-codec quality oracle. Separation score needs competing sources; ordinary IMF components are not independently meaningful speech sources. The paper states no frame-level human labels and significant computational cost.
papers.proposal: Retain exact per-IMF fitting error and summed-block reconstruction metrics now. Later validate perceptual measures on reconstructed speech in its original utterance context, using the same unchanged context for each method.

papers.title: Coupled Splines for Sparse Curve Fitting
papers.method: Fits two coordinate functions with rotation-invariant total-variation/group regularization of derivatives. Shared sparse knots and hybrid spline orders permit smooth regions and corners. Proves spline representer results for its stated periodic curve-fitting objective.
papers.evidence: 2D contour experiments; equal-knot comparison in Fig. 3 reports QFE 12.09 versus 153.47. Hybrid linear/cubic fits reduce knot counts in demonstrated contours.
papers.limit: Theorems concern the declared 2D periodic convex objective, not arbitrary AM-FM factorization or shortest speech programs. Nonperiodic speech boundaries and sparse knot payloads need separate treatment.
papers.proposal: Fit the real and imaginary parts of a demodulated analytic IMF as coupled envelopes with shared adaptive knots. Phase rotation rotates these coordinates, suggesting a natural use of rotation-invariant coupling. Count knot locations, both coefficient sets and carrier parameters.

papers.title: Learnable Empirical Mode Decomposition Based on Mathematical Morphology
papers.venue: SIAM Journal on Imaging Sciences; local author manuscript
papers.method: Replaces interpolation envelopes with dilation/erosion, opening/closing or Lasry-Lions constructions; learns structuring functions and convex envelope weights. Derives gradients through extrema and discusses additive-shift invariance of sifting.
papers.evidence: Toy 1D classification and hyperspectral classification (Indian Pines/Pavia), spatially disjoint train/test regions, ten repetitions. In the reported task the classifier uses residuals of a single decomposition step.
papers.limit: This demonstrates trainable morphological preprocessing, not compact speech reconstruction. Nonsmooth extrema have sparse gradients, and the representation need not satisfy classical IMF criteria merely because the module is called EMD.
papers.proposal: Use constrained learnable envelopes as an alternative decomposition arm. Validate sum/remainder, oscillatory properties and actual formula cost, and impose no uncharged raw-signal feature bypass.

papers.title: Neural Networks Fail to Learn Periodic Functions and How to Fix It
papers.method: Introduces Snake_a(x)=x+sin(a*x)^2/a, studies periodic extrapolation, monotonicity and initialization, and discusses learnable frequency.
papers.evidence: Synthetic periodic regression and other forecasting/classification examples. The extrapolation theorem is an existence result with sufficient width, not a finite-width optimization guarantee.
papers.limit: This is the original Snake paper, not a SnakeBeta paper. Extrapolation beyond a fitting interval differs from our exact sampled reconstruction task. A favorable neural activation does not establish the smallest standalone IMF formula.
papers.proposal: Allow Snake-like residual-periodic compositions as language elements, compare against their expanded elementary formulas, and separately test trainability versus final achievable error at matched parameter counts.

papers.title: Plug-and-play learnable EMD module for time-domain speech separation
papers.method: Uses max pooling on positive/negative signals and transposed convolutions for EMD-inspired features, which supplement an existing time-domain speech-separation encoder.
papers.evidence: Four two-speaker separation datasets and SI-SNR-based training; small extra model/compute cost. Feature analysis acknowledges learned outputs are not a complete implementation of original EMD envelopes.
papers.limit: Reported separation improvements do not establish a source-free compact decomposition. Equations label an envelope average as an IMF; distinguish the paper's feature construction from classical sifting. Existing raw-signal encoding remains part of the system.
papers.proposal: Borrow differentiable envelope estimation as an implementation option, but validate our output modes independently and ensure reconstruction uses only the explicitly stored mathematical representation.

papers.title: (Exhaustive) symbolic regression and model selection by minimum description length
papers.venue: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A
papers.method: Enumerates expressions within a declared operator set and maximum tree size, removes equivalences, fits constants, and ranks descriptions using structural, parameter-precision and residual terms.
papers.evidence: Benchmark and astrophysical applications. Describes a typical complexity-10 run of roughly 200 CPU hours. Shows different syntactic/parametric expressions can represent the same function; numerical tolerance still affects fitting.
papers.limit: Enumeration coverage is bounded by grammar and maximum complexity; local constant fitting does not become globally solved through enumeration. MDL depends on coding/model assumptions and operator vocabulary. Its statistical precision formula should not be transplanted blindly to noiseless speech coding.
papers.proposal: Add safe canonical simplification, remove redundant scale/constant parameters, and enumerate very small programs as a coverage reference. Keep parameter-count frontiers now and report actual representation cost separately; precision-aware coding can follow later without RVQ.

papers.title: WIRE: Wavelet Implicit Neural Representations
papers.method: Uses complex Gabor activations combining an oscillatory carrier and Gaussian localization. Discusses empirical NTK bias, real variants, scale/frequency choices and inverse problems.
papers.evidence: Images, 3D volumes, visual inverse problems and radiance fields. Counts real/imaginary weights in architecture comparisons by reducing complex network width.
papers.limit: Evidence is visual rather than few-parameter speech coding. Denoising biases can suppress noise-like speech detail. Network weights, complex components and localization parameters all count if used per IMF.
papers.proposal: Expose localized oscillatory atoms or compositions to symbolic discovery for transient modes. Compare full-frame oscillators with localized ones, including center, width, phase, frequency and envelope costs.

papers.title: Short-time variational mode decomposition
papers.method: Applies a short-time transform to VMD/MVMD. Non-dynamic version shares centers across windows; dynamic version lets them change with window while sharing within multichannel observations. Gives normalized window reconstruction and online handling.
papers.evidence: Synthetic stationary/nonstationary signals and SSVEP EEG; examples show a temporal/frequency-resolution tradeoff and increased computation. Authors discuss window/mode selection and noise sensitivity as limitations.
papers.limit: Not just independently running ordinary VMD on disjoint chunks. Short-time analysis still has endpoint extensions and window-resolution effects. No compact description optimization or speech coding result.
papers.proposal: Use it as a decomposition reference when returning to longer audio, with explicit mode tracking and normalized synthesis. Keep 40-ms isolated controls to separate fitting failure from stitching, while still measuring boundary-specific fitting error.

papers.title: Sinusoidal Frequency Estimation by Gradient Descent
papers.method: Optimizes real parts of complex powers, Re(z^n), allowing radial damping while the frequency angle moves; uses amplitude correction/refitting to recover a real sinusoid.
papers.evidence: N=4096, zero initial target phase, 50k steps for single tones and 300k for mixtures in the reported settings. Improves over direct real sinusoidal optimization; authors observe component collisions and missing quieter tones.
papers.limit: No formal general convergence result; not yet a general speech/chirped-AM-FM solution. Final error must be measured on the intended real expression, not the damped surrogate.
papers.proposal: Use damping as a temporary optimization aid, then restore/refit the transmitted real expression. Test random phases, chirps, weak components and 640-sample signals at practical budgets before adopting it.

papers.title: Differentiable Time-Varying Linear Prediction in the Context of End-to-End Analysis-by-Synthesis
papers.method: Derives efficient sample-wise time-varying LP backpropagation and integrates it with a source-filter synthesizer. Studies source/noise-filter coupling and reflection coefficient parameterization.
papers.evidence: 24-kHz VCTK, 2-second training segments, one million optimization steps. Subjective comparison uses two selected speakers, with 17 retained listeners; phase and pitch estimation affect results.
papers.limit: This is not free-form per-IMF function discovery. It demonstrates that frame-wise training and sample-wise evaluation can disagree; spectral error and subjective rankings need not agree.
papers.proposal: Use exactly the same formula evaluator in fitting and final reconstruction. Later test shared harmonic phase/source structure between modes as an explicit graph, storing all shared parameters, pointers and residual innovations.
